hook: Volunteers who drank caffeine reacted in 241 milliseconds on average; those who drank a caffeine-free look-alike took 262. Random assignment made the groups comparable, so if the gap is real, caffeine caused it. Is a 21 millisecond gap bigger than chance would produce? The two-sample t test answers that.

misconception.wrong: A p-value of 0.274 shows the two counties have the same mean exercise time.
misconception.right: A large p-value means the observed difference is the kind chance alone often produces. It is not convincing evidence of a difference, and it is not evidence that the means are equal.

summary: A two-sample t test computes $t = \frac{\bar{x}_1 - \bar{x}_2}{\sqrt{s_1^2/n_1 + s_2^2/n_2}}$, finds the p-value from the t distribution with technology or conservative df in the direction of $H_a$, and concludes about $\mu_1 - \mu_2$ in context. Random assignment allows a causal conclusion; random samples allow generalizing.
